message.content: In Christian theology, the focus is generally on Jesus Christ as the central figure—often referred to as the “Son of God” and the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies. However, many Christians also regard the prophets of the Hebrew Bible (such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others) as highly significant because they laid the groundwork for the covenantal relationship between God and humanity and foretold the coming of the Messiah. The idea of who is “most important” can vary depending on theological tradition, denominational emphasis, and individual belief. Some traditions emphasize the prophetic role of Jesus himself, while others highlight the foundational work of the Old Testament prophets.
